title: The Living Soul as the Second Field, Tilled from Above by the Two Great Luminaries
arc: The teaching identifies the purified Living Soul as a second ploughed-field set within the whole Zone of the upper place, and shows how the two great heavenly luminaries, exalted above her, do farmer's work upon her so that, moving toward the divine likeness, she is drawn upward to the Height.
reading:
This short teaching takes a single agricultural picture — a ploughed field with farmers exalted above it — and uses it to describe the condition of a soul that has already been refined and now stands free in the spiritual region above the natural cosmos. The "second ploughed-field" is the Living Soul, that is, Divine Truth which has been gathered out of the mingled state and is now being worked a second time, no longer for separation from darkness but for elevation. The first ploughing took place in the natural earth where seeds had to be sorted from weeds; this second ploughing takes place after that work is finished, in the open belt of heaven itself.

The site of this second tillage is named with precision: she is "established within the entire Zone of the upper place." The Zone is the cosmic girdle of states that holds the worlds in their order, and "the upper place" identifies the heavenly side of that girdle. So the soul here imagined is no longer submerged in the salt sea of natural affections; she has been lifted into the encompassing belt where the discrete degrees of heaven are arranged. She is fixed there as a field is fixed in the earth — a stable receptive ground, but a heavenly one.

Above her stand "two great luminaries," exalted over her and "doing farmer's work" upon her. In this corpus the two luminaries are the sun and the moon, the two ships of light: Divine Truth in its illuminating manifestation and Divine Truth in its receptive reflection. Together they form the conjunction by which all heavenly states are governed. To call them farmers is to say that the work of these two luminaries upon the elevated soul is the same as ploughing, sowing, and reaping: they break her open to influx, plant correspondences in her, and bring forth fruit. They are not external agents working from far away; they are the celestial pair whose joint shining is the very labour that cultivates her.

The purpose of their work is given in the phrase "toward the likeness they may move toward her." The likeness here is the icon — the true representational form of the Divine Human — which all redeemed light is meant to receive and resemble. The farmer-luminaries till the field so that her motion will be assimilated to that likeness; her every stirring under their light is a stirring toward the divine image. Once she is moving in that direction, she is "drawn upward," she "comes unto the Height," and she "goes forth" through the upper place. This is the regular vocabulary of regenerative ascent: the soul, once aligned with the icon, does not stay in any one heaven but is conveyed upward through the discrete degrees toward the inmost.

The closing line, "in every place where she is within them; and they reckon toward them," seals the teaching with a note of mutual indwelling. The luminaries are above her, but she is also within them; wherever the soul is found held within their light, that very location becomes a place from which ascent occurs. Their reckoning toward her — their attention, their counting her as their own — is what guarantees that the upward motion does not fail.

Read as a whole, the teaching is a picture of the state that follows purification. The soul that has been separated from the mingling is not left passive in heaven; she becomes a field for a higher cultivation, worked by the conjoined sun and moon of Divine Truth, and by their labour she is continually moved toward the likeness of the Divine and conveyed upward through the Zone toward the Height. The lacunae do not damage this arc; the surviving phrases give the field, the farmers above her, the likeness as goal, the drawing upward, and the Height as destination — the complete spiritual movement.
